Messages.Author: wumpus
Messages.Body:
Howdy,

Hypothetical situation, in a sanctioned tournament:

A -> B -> C -> D -> E ->

A ousts B, and looks strong enough to possibly sweep. E offers a deal
to D: help me oust A and C and I will roll. D accepts and A and C
are successfully ousted.

Can E now concede?

I thought that the new tournament rules said, in effect, that all
deals were off when the table was reduced to two players, and that
each must play to win, but the discussion in the English Nationals
thread seems to indicate that the concession rules take precedence
(i.e. a player can concede at any point as long as everyone else
remaining at the table agrees).

Or is it the special circumstances in that case (finals table,
conceding player in a 'lost' position) that make keeping the deal in
that case kosher? (If the latter, then I suppose E just had to play
with no regards to defense while ousting A and C, so that she is in a
'lost' position when the endgame is reached.)

Wonderin',
Alex

Messages.Body:

>
> A ousts B, and looks strong enough to possibly sweep. E offers a deal
> to D: help me oust A and C and I will roll. D accepts and A and C
> are successfully ousted.

At this point:
A: 1VP
B: 0
C: 0
D: 0
E: 2 VP

> Can E now concede?

Not if it isn't PTW.

He can concede if he's in a truly lost position (unable to get any more VPs).

> I thought that the new tournament rules said, in effect, that all
> deals were off when the table was reduced to two players, and that
> each must play to win,

Correct.

I would assume that in this context "unable to get any more VPs" must
include "unable to survive until time out thereby gaining a half VP
and a game win." I would assume it would not be permissible to adopt
the perspective of unlimited time, and thereby project one's own
ultimate defeat, and concede on that basis.

Messages.Author: Bram Vink
Messages.Body:

> ultimate defeat, and concede on that basis.-

It does include that. The consideration is only: Can you do better
than you have? so in preliminary rounds, strive for GW, else maximize
VPs. This includes timeout half VP, though keep in mind stalling is
illegal, and in final rounds you have to strive to maximize your
standing.
Before the last two the rule is: It is legal to keep deals that were
play to win at the time you made them. As soon as you reach those last
two, that rule is off.

Cheers,
Bram
